gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-kodchasan: Marker-bold and sunlit. Red Hat Display draws punchy headings, while Kodchasan, a plain sans with open-hanging terminals, handles the quieter text work.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-koho: Confident, marker-like strokes lead the way in Red Hat Display, with light showing inside every curve. And KoHo follows in a sans-serif with wide c openings, so a long passage moves along without any crowding.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-kosugi: Loud, marker-thick headings meet a wire-bent text face, the pliers-like open c of Kosugi running through every word. Red Hat Display and this plain sans simply sit well together.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-kulim-park: Kulim Park keeps its terminals the width they began, friendly and unfussy beneath a bold marker-line heading. Kulim Park's gentle openness against Red Hat Display's contemporary punch is what makes the pair work.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-kumbh-sans: Bold, marker-like lines with daylight in every curve define Red Hat Display, and Kumbh Sans, a plain sans with terminals cut short of the bowl, carries the text. Pen-drawn and steady, it holds up over a long passage.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-lato: A single, unvarying line gives Red Hat Display its marker-like punch. And Lato, a sans with wide, barely curled s curves, sits beside it softer and quieter.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-libre-franklin: Contemporary through and through, Red Hat Display lays its spaghetti-like line out in confident letters. But it earns its keep big and short, while Libre Franklin, a plain sans with a splayed c terminal, takes over the text.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-livvic: Friendly and clean, Livvic lets its curves run without stress, with a generous opening in the c. Red Hat Display is best at bold, marker-line headings, while Livvic does its best work as an approachable sans-serif body.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-lunasima: Lunasima reads clean and contemporary, its c tips never creeping toward touching. And beneath Red Hat Display's neon-tube headings, a long passage in this plain sans would move along comfortably.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-m-plus-1p: M PLUS 1p keeps every curve end open, tidy and neutral as a sans body. Red Hat Display earns its keep big and short, where even its w shows no thick or thin strokes.
